properties.name: La Cumbre - Colima
properties.takeoff_description: Take-off is oriented SSW. Ideal take-off varies between 10:00 and 14:00 hours, depending on local conditions and seasonal changes. Take-off itself is located at the top of La Cumbre at 750 m (above sea level) 350 mts from ground.Optimal flying conditions has a breeze that comes from the sea, which is located about 40 km (25 miles) away in a straight line in a SSE direction, and the valleys in front of take-off generate optimal thermal conditions.
properties.flight_rules: 10 miles north is the Colima airport, it is not allowed to fly in that direction.
properties.going_there: Upon reaching Colima, go to the Hotel Costeño, which is out point of reunion, and is located at 1001 Carlos de la Madrid Bejar Boulevard (see the map section Ander Lodging). Once there, take the highway towards Jiquilpan. At the first kilometer (slightly more that half a mile) there will be a concrete police shack on your right-hand side. After another 3 kilometers (almost 2 miles) there is a small bridge overlooking the El Salado. One more kilometer (about half a mile) and on your right there is the entrance road to the village of Piscila, the landing zone in front of take-off. If you are going directly to take-off, do not turn in here, but continue on the highway. Two more kilometers (1.25 miles) alter passing the entrance to the crossroads (Jiquilpan-Piscila), there is an cobblestone road to the right of the highway (it appears just as one comes around a curve). There is a concrete shack on the left-side of this entrance and a white metal cattle-gate (usually open, but not locked if closed). There is only one cobblestone road and will lead directly to take-off. Once there one will see a large rectangular concrete structure for holding water with a chapel at the far end, topped by a statue of the Virgin.
properties.comments:
It is forbidden flying directly North of take-off, there is a national airportthere (restricted flying zone). At take-off, next to the door to the chapel, there is a printed map where one may observe the restricted zone and other details.
Flying at La Cumbre has both thermal and soaring conditions. There is a range of mountains in a slight horseshoe shape that is located SE of take-off, which provides for convection, and over the valley of Piscila and Colima there are strong thermals. During December (the time of out competition) the thermal ceilings may easily reach more than 2500 m ASL (8250 feet). Ideal take-off varies between 11:00 and 14:00 hours, depending on local conditions and seasonal changes. One may fly about 85% of the year in Colima with good conditions.

properties.name: La Malinche
properties.takeoff_description:
La Malinche Launch is unique in the region; the intersection of three valleys releases a consistent daily house thermal. It is the best local launch for both local and XC flights, providing options for 360 degrees and landing zones in all directions, as well as an extensive system of inexpensive taxis to take you where you wish. 
Pilots new to this site should get a briefing of the multiple landing and XC options. 
The large grass launch is maintained year around exclusively for paragliding by the paragliding owners and can easily accommodate 4 – 5 gliders.  
Winds are predictably Southwest, South, and Southeast.
Top landings are common for local Mexican tandem pilots and should present no problems for intermediate pilots.
properties.flight_rules:
No regulations
Air traffic is very rare.
Flying is prohibited directly over the rectangular military base 7 kilometers to the northeast, identifiable by a large Mexican flag at the entrance. 
Avoid unharvested fields and stay as far away from fields with livestock, especially horses, as much as is possible.
properties.going_there:
La Malinche flight park is just a few kilometers south of Tenancingo on the road to Acatzingo.  
Taxis can be taken from Tenancingo de Degollado  to launch road head, which is a  4WD or strong 2WD access, or it is a 20 minute walk.
A $50 pesos site development donation per pilot per day is to help Daniel with development. Transportation is $50 pesos. Pilots meet at Casadelpiloto house at 104 Mariann Matamoros Sur, Tenancingo.
properties.comments:
The flight park has a  pilot's building with 2 basic hotel rooms with hot/cold water, showers, toilet and shared kitchen.La Malinche Flight Park has a onsite pilot's building with 2 basic hotel rooms with hot/cold water, showers, toilet and a shared kitchen.
Casa Del Piloto, located in Tenancingo, is an English speaking lodge that provides comfortable accommodations for up to 9 pilots. The host also offers paragliding transport and tours. See www.casadelpiloto.com or contact casadelpiloto@gmail.com for more details.  Low Season rentals (April – September) are also available by request.
properties.weather:
The flying season in this region is excellent in the winter and spring months, and we get rain in the summer afternoons but it is still flyable on dry days.  The launch site is situated directly in front of one of the most consistent house thermals in the whole region of several valleys.  

Late October - November - Gentle thermals, 2800 - 3100 m- 90% - good for beginner under instruction, XC, Ridge soaring, 90% flyable every day

December -January - Med-strong thermals 2800 - 3800 m - XC, Ridge soaring, Magic Air- 98% flyable everyday.

February - March - Med Strong thermals 5000+ m - XC, Ridge soaring, Magic Air- 98% flyable everyday.

landing.landing_description:
The Cabanas (Cabins) Piano LZ is located to the left below a clearing North of 3 cabins. This LZ is NOT recommended for mid-day flights, due to a thermal trigger below Launch.
The Road Piano LZ is below Launch to the right and runs North-South to the village below. 
 
There are trials from both LZs backup to Launch; these can be walked in less than 40 minutes. The Cabanas LZ trail is located to the right of the fence.  It follows the ridgeline uphill, then heads to the right, above the cows and water holding pool.

properties.name: El Picacho - Malinalco
properties.takeoff_description: A part of beautiful grass covered sheep grazing pastures, a south-east facing launch with the wind usually crossing 45 degrees from the right.  There is a also a true south facing alternate further on down the trail from launch.  It is a rather steep launch.
properties.going_there: Arrive at the little pueblo of El Picacho at the north end of the Malinalco Valley.  There is a road leading downhill that cuts off the main highway in front of a little store called El Parapente.  You may park your vehical down at the end of that road, and pay the local kids a few pesos to 'watch' your vehical.  From there you walk down a little path through the pastures about one kilometer to launch.  The locals know where it is.
properties.comments: Marco Guillermo also pays the rent on the best training hill in the region, near the base of launch.

landing.landing_description:
Land on the piano shaped field. Watch for a barbed wire fence running East to West across it. 

Pack and walk to main highway

---
There are a number of open agricultural fields at the base of launch, any which one that is not planted should be suitable for landing.  The one place you should NOT land is in the country club at the base of launch, as your wing will be confiscated if you land there.

properties.name: Yelapa Tapita
properties.takeoff_description: Carpeted launch with shade shelter, thorny brush surrounding carpeted area is unforgiving of aborted launches or errant launches.
properties.flight_rules: $5 US per day to fly; $50 seasonal membership paid to local gringo pilot. No local radio frequency established.
properties.going_there: Arrive in Yelapa by water taxi from Puerto Vallarta.  Walk up dirt trail from town to launch in about 20 minutes. No cars in Yelapa.
properties.comments: An ideal car-free paragliding destination.  Winds are usually light and cross in morning and straighten out before noon. Stronger winds in afternoon enable ridge soaring.  A fairly mellow and straightforward flying site.
properties.weather: Dependent upon sea breeze for flying.  Thermals are generally light but can also be turbulent at moments.

landing.landing_description: Long sandy beach with lagoon on backside, bars & restaurants & sunbathers on beach.

properties.name: Yelapa Tapa
properties.takeoff_description: Cleared area near ridgetop where power lines leave ridge for Yelapa.  Two launch spots possible for slightly different wind directions (E & NNE).  Short runway with steep drop-off requires decent launch skills.
properties.going_there: Arrive in Yelapa by water taxi from Puerto Vallarta. Walk up pathways & a dirt trail from town to parking area near cemetery.  You can hike the road (1.5 hours) to launch, hike a trail that is shorter & shadier, or hire a pickup truck ride for $10 per person from local pilot(25 minutes to launch). No cars in the town of Yelapa itself.
properties.comments: Prevailing afternoon winds are from the west which is over the back. Most launches happen mid-morning when thermals begin to blow upslope on the front side, temporarily overpowering the prevailing winds.
properties.weather: Opposing winds above launch, variable upslope and over-the-back cycles on launch.

landing.landing_description: Long sandy beach with lagoon on backside, bars & restaurants & sunbathers on beach. Same LZ as for Yelapa Tapita.

properties.name: Valle de Bravo - El Peñon
properties.takeoff_description:
One of the best flying sites in Mexico (and probably in the world). During the months of December to March the conditions allow for flights on the 100's km order, with cloud bases of 4,500 plus meters msl.
The launch was expanded on 2008 by the government of the Estado de Mexico as part of the improvements for the Mexico 2009 Paragliding World Championship.
properties.flight_rules: written in a board on take off and landing
properties.going_there: Take the road from Valle de Bravo to Temascaltepec and turn right in the Albarrada road sign. Follow the signs on the dirt road to the launch.
properties.weather:
From February to the beginning of the rain season the conditions get stronger, with rough air and strong winds almost all day.
During the rain season conditions are mellow, but there is risk of fast overdeveloping, with strong thunderstorms.

landing.landing_description: The official landing is a big grass field 2.5km in front of the launch. The favorite cross country flight is in the direction of Valle de Bravo, to land on the lakeside landing of Santa Maria, 14km to the NNW.

properties.name: Teta Azul de la Misión
properties.takeoff_description: The launch site is located ten minutes past Playa Santtispac and is accessed via a well marked and two wheel drive gravel road on your right. The best launch is 25 feet north of the gate to the antenna and just below the road. The prevailing winds are from the east which creates a slight side hill launch situation. If the winds clock to the north then you can lay your wing at the edge of the road and you will have a very clear and level launching path right toward the LZ.
properties.going_there:
About 75 minutes north of Loreto just east of Highway 1.
Lat: 26.848789
Lon: -111.903176
properties.comments: There are guy wires to the north and south of the launch area but they do not obstruct launch in any way. If you are ridge soaring then a couple of wings could comfortably fly between these two obstructions. Because of the east facing slope thermal flying will end in the middle of the afternoon but ridge soaring will still be possible.

landing.landing_description:
The LZ is access via a gravel road just 2 or 3 minutes past the turnoff to the antenna. Again, this is two wheel drive accessible and will get your vehicle to with 200 feet of the beach. The parking area is also the best landing area and there is plenty of room for both. Landing on the beach either near the parking area or closer to the antenna is a good option although you will need to make a crosswind final with a very short turn into the wind right before touchdown.

If you leave the mountain within 100 feet of launch, you should have no problem making it to the parking area LZ. If you scratch down lower then a bailout beach landing will be required with a five minute walk back to the parking area.

properties.name: Concha Chinas
properties.takeoff_description: This is an afternoon site and needs a sea breeze with some South in it.  While the launch has been improved, it is small without a bail-out option.  You need a breeze to be able to launch with only a few steps.  Jungle surrounds the launch.  You will need solid launching skills, this is not a launch for beginners.
properties.going_there: The trail to launch exists, but it is overgrown a bit and can be obscured by vegitation.  You want a local guide to lead you up to launch. You do not want to bush whack as the vegitation is too nasty to get through with a pack. Contact Victor at Hotel Rio, 322-222-0366, a local pilot who has repaired the launch site.
properties.comments: This site has both ridge lift and thermals.  The thermals may require active flying.
properties.weather: You will need the right cycle/breeze to launch. Make sure you can penetrate the breeze to avoid landing in the jungle.

landing.landing_description: You will be landing on the beach.  While there is a beach below launch, the hotel there is not very pilot friendly.  It is better to land on the beach at:  20Â° 36' 21.38' N 105Â° 14' 17.46 W.  You will need to crab your landing a bit, land on the beach dodging people and then if your spot landing is good, you will not get wet and your wing will land on the dry sand.  You should be able to make this LZ if you leave the flying area at the launch altitude.

properties.name: Tulum
properties.takeoff_description:
To fly the Mayan ruins of Tulum, you have to go by walk on the public beach which is situated 500 meters south of the ruins.
When you arrive at the end of the beach, there is some flat rocks before the small clifs and the lighthouse.
The best way to fly there is to inflate the glider on the beach and to walk in direction of the lighthouse. If the wind is in the good direction you will takeoff easily. BE CAREFULL, it's for expert pilot only!!! No landing place between the beach and the ruins and it's forbiden to land in the ruins or on the beach down the ruins...
properties.flight_rules: I'm not sure the flight is always allowed by mexican's autorities and Tulum ruins security. Ask informations to local people
properties.going_there: From Tulum city, take the road to the Mayan's ruins and stop the car at the public beach before the ruins
properties.comments:
EXPERT PILOTS ONLY... You need very good skills to takeoff behind the rocks and there is no landing place down the cliff. the ocean is rough and there is only rocks...
VIDEO : https://vimeo.com/63196255
properties.weather: You need the perfect wind direction to fly there (east or south-east) and at least 20 km/h. The wind is often strong...

landing.landing_description: On the public beach (BE CAREFULL with the people, the sea and the rocks...)

properties.name: El Toro Bull Hill
properties.takeoff_description:
Takeoff (despegue) is just to the east of the top T intersection at the top of the mountain below the antennas.

There is a north facing takeoff at the helipad higher up near the west antennas.
properties.flight_rules: ZLO control zone is 5 kms north of the Antennas and there is an airway from Manzanillo airport to Colima Airport that is 4000 feet ASL to 18000 feet.
properties.going_there:
Drive north from Manzanillo to La Central. At the north end of La Central there is a sand road that heads east from the highway. Stay on that road and you will hit a black metal gate and stay on the main road all the way to the top.

Please close gates as you go through as there are cattle grazing on the road.
properties.comments: You need a truck with good traction as some parts of the road are steep and sandy.

properties.name: Tepoztlan
properties.takeoff_description: Located in San Juan Tlacotenco. Launch is oriented south bound, approximately 700 meters above landing
properties.flight_rules: none
properties.going_there: Tepoztlan is located one hour drive south from Mexico City. You can either go by bus or car rental.
properties.comments:
The best time to launch is before 11:00am to avoid strong thermal conditions which can be rather rough, specially during summer. You can also flight after 4:00 pm once that stronger winds are dying out.

The views are beautiful with interest rock formations and the valley above. If you are lucky you can see the Popo and Izta volcanoes from the distance
properties.weather: Strong winds and thermals during noon. It is important to launch knowing the wind direction to avoid lee side where you are likely to find rotors.

landing.landing_description:
Located beside the football field in Santo Domingo, Tepoztlan. Usually the approach and landing is East - SouthEast bound.

Mind the electricity lines and houses sorroundind the landing field. You can often find some air bubbles and lift as you approach landing. Be prepared to spend some time over the approach before loosing altitude.

properties.name: La Jolla
properties.takeoff_description: Park at the base of the mountain across from the pond. Hike up about half way up to a barely improved patch cleared by the local pilots. Not for faint of heart ;)
properties.flight_rules: Respect the locals and don’t leave trash or plastic bottles behind you.
properties.going_there: Take the road to Recreativo "Joya-La Barreta" Park. Keep going on the cobbles stone road till you see a pond on your left side and a grass parking on your right.
properties.comments: It’s a nice place to ridge soar in the evening or fly cross country. But a small hike is required and the takeoff is not friendly to novice pilots.
properties.weather: Typically flyable during the dry season aka winter.

properties.name: Tangano
properties.takeoff_description: Cleared areas at the top of the ridge. Have to hike up about 15 min from the base of the ridge. So no park in the unpaved area due to risk for tire damage form construction waste.
properties.flight_rules: Queretaro airport is west of this site and GA aircraft can sometimes fly near this site.
properties.going_there: Park near intersection under the electronic billboard. Hike up using the existing trail.
properties.comments: Nice area for easy ridge soaring in the evenings. Some turbulence exists from high rise buildings to the left of take off and low hanging high voltage lines are present just past that point as well.
properties.weather: Usually prevailing winds during the dry season in winter.

properties.takeoff_description: Due to road conditions a truck with 4x4 and high ground clearance is best. Car is possible but may need to hike the final stretch.
properties.going_there: When going up, close the gates behind you to prevent livestock from escaping.
